reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Receipts before reverence", "body": "Chance Garton opens by refusing to treat Kabbalah as a pure divine transmission. He points out that the Sefer Raziel HaMalakh, the Bahir and the Zohar leave no extant trail past the 13th century, and wonders aloud whether the system's emergence is tangled with the fall of the Templars, who employed Jewish clerks and bookkeepers. He then shows two diagrams, the 1516 Portae Lucis with only 17 paths instead of 22, and Athanasius Kircher's 1652 Oedipus Aegyptiacus. A Jesuit publishing Jewish mysticism inside a book on Egypt reads to him as fingerprints of the Therapeutae."}, {"title": "Daath and the tunnels of Set", "body": "Mario Garza came back to the Tree of Life because of one point on it, Daath, the hidden sephirah that Kabbalists call crossing the abyss. He read Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden at Juan's suggestion and found the whole shadow system, the Qliphothic tree of death, mapped not as paths but as tunnels of Set. Grant frames it as universe A and universe B, with this world birthed from that one, and Mario notes that modern magicians work Lovecraft's old ones as a live pantheon there. Chance adds that Daath is philologically Thoth, the crossroads, Hermes."}, {"title": "Everything points north", "body": "Mario's long running thread is the northern sky, and he was struck to find the same claim stated flatly in the Qliphothic material, that Daath is north. In that tradition Ursa Major is a primordial mother bear with seven children, Set is her eighth, and Sirius the dog star is identified with Set as well. He ties this to the central pillar of the tree, which always runs taller than the masculine and feminine pillars beside it, to Polaris as the nail star or sky nail, and to the eye and stairway on Freemasonic tracing boards."}, {"title": "Chance's word weaves", "body": "Chance runs philology as evidence for a single old system spread outward. He reads Adam Kadmon through QDM, the Hebrew root for east and sun, which gives Kadmos bringing 17 Phoenician letters to Greece and Kodam as a name of Buddha, and lands on Keter, Kronos, the horn and the crown. Chokmah he treats as cognate to Sophia, and to Arabic Hikmah and Hakeem, a wise man and also a physician, which loops back to the Therapeutae. He derives Eve from the Tetragrammaton, links Gilgul Neshamot to Golgotha and the whirlwind, and notes Eve encodes five, five, five."}, {"title": "What happens when we die", "body": "Asked bluntly, Chance says he honestly has no clue, then offers that life is an idea so intense we forget it is an idea, and that death is less a journey than someone snapping their fingers beside us. Mario answers with the circumpunct, a circle with a dot, feminine cosmos holding a masculine point, which he reads as Polaris and the world axis. Both resist escapist ascension. Chance connects the trapped sparks of Isaac Luria's Tikkun Olam to the Buddhist claim that clinging causes suffering, and warns that the real danger in any of it is dogma."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies returns to InnerVerse for a deep dive into the componentry of the system of Kabbalah. What is the tree of life, and what are its Sefirot? Does the system have ancient roots, or is it a relatively modern contrivance? And what is the Qliphoth, the inverted tree of death, and how is it used in magical working?

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Typhon Current and the Cult of the Mother", "body": "Mario opens the members hour arguing that the swastika has been suppressed for its northern connections, then names the tradition standing behind the Qliphothic tree. Typhon here is not the Greek masculine monster but the primordial dark mother, which Chance immediately glosses as Tiamat. Mario lists the aliases modern practitioners use, the Typhon tradition, the Lovecraftian current, the Setian line, Kenneth Grant's stellar mythos and the cult of the mother. Chance adds that Nag Hammadi itself means dark serpent mother, and that Typhon read right to left hides oph, the serpent, so the whole current is a serpent mother tradition."}, {"title": "The Northern Sky Read as the Underworld", "body": "The slides turn Ursa Major into a weapon. Mario presents the adze and the khopesh as substitute symbols for the seven stars, the iron of Set, the blade Set used to cut his way out of his mother, and notes the adze held to the pharaoh's mouth in the opening of the mouth ritual. Chance supplies the hieroglyph behind khopesh, which means leg, and the Dendera zodiac showing the Big Dipper as a thigh. Mario then walks through Taweret, the hippopotamus goddess tied to Draco, seven dots in her headdress, a knife in her hand and a severed leg set across from her."}, {"title": "The Shadow Side of the Tarot", "body": "Mario explains that the tunnels of Set number twenty two, matching the paths, the major arcana and the Hebrew letters, and that Lon Milo Duquette hid a tunnel sigil in the corner of every card of his deck, one disease per tunnel. Mario has never worked with reversals; Chance says reversals are worth it and describes drawing cards before a biofield tuning session to find the shape of a client's conditioning. From there Chance argues that life is a giant live action role play, that the danger is not the game but forgetting you are playing, and that language is the scaffolding you either climb or stay beneath."}, {"title": "Kabbalah Smuggled Into Pop Culture", "body": "Chance revives an old research project on Final Fantasy VII, where the villain is named Sephiroth, his alien mother is Jenova, which he hears as Jehovah, and the fighter Tifa carries the name of Tiferet, the emanation of beauty. The city of Midgar is a wheel of eight sectors around a central tower, and because one sector is destroyed in the story it ends as seven sections around one tower, a sevenfold city like Troy or Mount Meru. Mario answers with the World Tree, which he says is the Tree of Life under another name, and points to Avatar as the clearest modern example."}, {"title": "Phylacteries, Necromancy and the Return of All Things", "body": "Chance introduces the phylactery, the amulet that in fantasy holds a fragment of a soul outside the body, and asks whether scripture worn in a leather box does the same work, keeping an entity alive on the attention of worshippers. Mario answers with the tefillin, seven wraps of the band around the arm, the black cube worn on the head, and the seven circuits of the black cube at Mecca. Chance closes the loop: daimon in Greek meant the spirits of the dead, and God can only be perfect if everything that ever was eventually returns exactly as it was."}]
